reason: E1 supports phosphorus aiding amorphization, but only in general metallic glasses, not specifically in the claimed CrMnFeCoNiP system. E2 and E3 discuss carbon shell stabilization and carbon doping in laser-synthesized Cantor alloy nanoparticles, but do not involve phosphorus or demonstrate improved glass-forming ability and thermal stability in bulk alloys. The key premise that carbon doping increases configurational entropy and shifts Tg/Tx is not directly evidenced.
premises: Phosphorus addition supports amorphization in high-entropy alloys

Carbon doping reduces atomic mobility and suppresses crystallization
